args.rationale: Governing-law scoping for Contract 2 (Ferrand & Slate advisory engagement) under the firm's UCC Article 2 scope memo (matter document 192). The contract is a clean service contract: Halcyon engages Ferrand & Slate Partners to study and redesign its warehouse picking workflow, deliver a written recommendations report, and coach floor supervisors through implementation, for a $54,000 professional fee. Ferrand & Slate sells no equipment and transfers title to nothing except the paper report embodying its advice; the entire subject of the engagement is advisory and design labor. Under memo Section 1, the common law governs contracts for services, consulting, design, and advisory work, and Section 2 confirms that a contract whose entire subject is advisory work is governed by the common law even where the provider incidentally delivers paper materials. There is no goods price allocation, so the hybrid/predominant-purpose test is inapplicable — and the incidental paper report is trivial material that does not convert the engagement into a sale of goods. Accordingly, UCC Article 2 does NOT govern Contract 2; the common law governs it. Recorded as the negative (rejected) disposition.
